clue.text: Current problem about to restrict favourite's momentum

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece encloses the other
about tells us to turn the word for problem round

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a pet is a favourite; the 's reads as 'is' and adds no letters

explanation.surface: An electrical fault threatens to hold back a front-runner's momentum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like part of the electrical picture but just gives the symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is a synonym for momentum, the driving force behind movement.

clue.text: Home Rule might be appropriate

parts.note: in means at home
an order is a rule or command

explanation.surface: Irish Home Rule might be fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: Home Rule was self-government for Ireland, a long-running British political issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in order is proper, fitting or appropriate.

clue.text: Venomous creature seen in box one musician keeps hidden

indicators.note: the musician holds the other letters hidden inside

parts.note: a piper is a musician who plays pipes
the box is informal for television, TV
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A snake shows up on television, though a musician keeps it out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Pit vipers are venomous snakes, like rattlesnakes, with heat-sensing pits.

clue.text: That is nothing an idiot will admit

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the idiot takes in the letter

parts.note: a twit is a fool
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: That's nothing a fool will own up to.
explanation.definitionFit: That is, or namely, is the meaning of this old legal phrase used before a clarification.

clue.text: Star has depressing experience after drink

parts.note: the sun is a star
a downer is something depressing

explanation.surface: A celebrity has a bad time after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset.

clue.text: Bird shelters exist in eastern highland region

indicators.note: a bird that shelters something holds it inside itself

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: Birds find shelter in a mountainous part of the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is the high plateau region of eastern Asia, the Roof of the World.

clue.text: Hip replacement for the queen arranged, say, finally

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A hip replacement for the Queen was arranged, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip replacement' reads as surgery, but 'Hip' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip is slang for fashionable or up to date, which is trendy.

clue.text: Expert oilman oddly heading north for port on East Coast

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means read upwards, backwards
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A skilled oil worker behaves strangely, heading north to an Eastern port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks OLA from 'oilman', and 'heading north' turns it into ALO.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is a lake port in New York State, in the eastern United States.

clue.text: He abandons the league match

indicators.note: abandons means these letters leave the following word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
to league is to join together, to ally

explanation.surface: A man walks out of the league fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To tally is to match or correspond, as accounts that tally.

clue.text: Snobbish resort I had repeatedly left

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, putting letters in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word comes twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A posh holiday spot I kept on leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a holiday place but means re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Affectedly genteel or pretentious, the mannered speech of a snob.

clue.text: Loves contributing to a paper doing the rounds

indicators.note: the loves go into the other words, contributing to them from within

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
love is zero in tennis, written O, so two of them make OO

explanation.surface: Romantic letters to a newspaper are going round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afoot is astir and circulating, as a rumour doing the rounds is.

clue.text: Ace flew round when sent flying

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A fighter ace flew a loop after being sent into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Ace is informal praise meaning excellent, a synonym of marvellous.

clue.text: Max Ernst possibly Pop Artist? Not right

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father

indicators.note: not means the following letters are left out of the word before

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Was Max Ernst a Pop artist? Surely not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' removes RT from ARTIST, leaving AIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was one example of a member of the Dada art movement, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Wife oddly resolved to pen note

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the note sits inside
something resolved is worked out anew, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
la is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A wife strangely decided to write a short letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like an instruction to take odd letters, but it is the anagram fodder: 'resolved' turns it into OLDDY, and 'to pen' puts LA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: My old lady is informal slang for one's wife.

clue.text: US lawyer stumbling across judge in part of India

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney in the US

indicators.note: across means the first word is laid across the letter for judge, holding it

parts.note: reeling means staggering, stumbling about

explanation.surface: An American attorney trips over a judge somewhere in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Darjeeling is a hill town and district of West Bengal, famous for tea.

clue.text: Food served up in green room, primarily cheese

indicators.note: in places the turned food inside the other letters

parts.note: lime is a shade of green

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means placed going upwards, backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter

explanation.surface: A meal is brought up in the green room, mainly cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The green room is a theatre's waiting room, but here green and room are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Limburger is a soft, notoriously smelly Belgian cheese.

clue.text: Unknown individual's belt

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns
one is a single individual; the 's reads as 'is' and adds no letters

explanation.surface: A stranger's belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is a band of territory, as in the Sun Belt, so a region or area.

clue.text: Deplore judge supporting senior manager

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: an exec is an executive
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: Condemn a judge who backs a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to detest or curse, a strong form of deploring.

clue.text: One said originally to possess hard grip

indicators.note: to possess is to hold, so the letter is held within
originally here means in an original, new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone first claimed to have a firm hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is the state of sticking fast to a surface, which gives a grip.

clue.text: Great writer needs energy to replace old ending

indicators.note: to replace means one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: Victor Hugo was a French writer
O is the abbreviation for old, and it also stands at the end of the writer's name
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A great author needs fresh energy to rework an old ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Great in its sense of very large, enormous or immense.

clue.text: Primate, finding question hard, possessing zero answer

indicators.note: possessing means holding the next letter inside

parts.note: to grill is to question hard
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: An ape, grilled on a question, has nothing to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas are the largest of the great apes, which are primates.

clue.text: Presumption about Republican's lack of discretion

indicators.note: about means going round the letter that follows

parts.note: presumption is cheek, insolence, impudence
R stands for Republican; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A Republican's arrogance shows his indiscretion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of discretion is a straight paraphrase of rashness or unwisdom.

clue.text: Record number following new God

indicators.note: following puts the record and number after the letter for new

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a number is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A record number comes after a new god.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the Roman god of the sea.

clue.text: Do a favour for unnamed peer, investing one grand

indicators.note: investing means surrounding as if clothing, putting letters inside
unnamed means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a peer is a noble
I is the Roman numeral one
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Help a nameless lord who puts up a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' takes N from NOBLE, leaving OBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to help them out, do a kindness.

clue.text: Canadian natives getting Cuba and Rio confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Indigenous Canadians mix up Cuba and Rio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canadian natives' suggests people, but these natives are North American reindeer; the plural is the same as the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: These reindeer are native animals of Canada's north, hence natives.

clue.text: Share that is for a pretty girl

parts.note: a cut is a share, as of profits
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A share of the takings for an attractive young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutie is informal for an attractive person, especially a young woman.

clue.text: One's used to clean defending from this player?

definitions.meaning: a brush or machine used to clear floors of dust
in football, a defender who plays behind the back line clearing up

explanation.surface: A cleaner, and a footballer who defends.
explanation.walkthrough: In football the sweeper is a free defender positioned behind the rest of the defence.
explanation.definitionFit: One device for cleaning and one football defensive role share this name.

clue.text: Brief opportunity to overcome resistance

indicators.note: to overcome is to come over something, so the word sits around the letter

parts.note: a shot is a chance or opportunity
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A fleeting chance to defeat the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief and short are synonyms describing something of little length.

clue.text: Pupil finally stops enjoying lecture

indicators.note: the letter stops up a gap in the phrase, sitting inside it

parts.note: taking to something is coming to like it

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A student at last stops enjoying the lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' puts L, the end of 'Pupil', inside TAKING TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down or scolding is a reprimand delivered at length, a lecture.

clue.text: Language that's divine (one time only)

indicators.note: one of the two Ts is removed, so time appears once only
one of the two Ts is removed, so time appears once only

parts.note: to divine is to guess or perceive, to intuit

explanation.surface: A language said to be divine, if only for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: '(one time only)' keeps just one of the two Ts in INTUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit is the language of the Inuit people of the Arctic, also called Inuktitut.

clue.text: Steer clear of old nurse injecting drugs? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: injecting means putting one piece inside another
quite the opposite reverses who goes into whom, so the drugs enclose the nurse

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so two Es are drugs
a VAD was a Voluntary Aid Detachment nurse in the World Wars

explanation.surface: Avoid an aged nurse who is shooting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' flips 'injecting', so the drugs go round the nurse rather than into her.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer clear of something is to avoid or dodge it.

clue.text: Following couple around in part of army

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the army unit

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

indicators.note: around turns the word for couple backwards

parts.note: to couple is to join or unite

explanation.surface: A pair reverse direction within an army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a link word but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A following is a group of attendants or supporters, which is a retinue.
